statement: A regression test must select its subject by the property under test, not by incidental ordering, index, fixture position or current registry shape.
classification: Child implementation rule under CI-2026-08-03-CANARY-REPRODUCES-DEFECT-001 — operator-added 2026-08-03. Not a peer invariant; it is how the parent is satisfied in test code.

canaries.assertion: no test in this file selects a registry subject by array index, and the three repaired sites select by semantic predicate (ratifiedSource === null, status === 'candidate')

occurrences.defect: 'a candidate self-promoted to ratified is REFUSED' selected registry.candidates[0]. When the operator ratified ACTOR-SUBJECT-OWNER, the record sorting first became validly ratified, so the mutation carried a legitimate ratifiedSource and the test stopped exercising self-promotion entirely — while still passing.
'flags a candidate with NO canary' modelled its synthetic on registry.candidates[0], which became a ratified record — a different subject from the candidate-stage records the check reasons about.

'a resolution at candidate with no compressed rule is a BLOCKER' selected registry.records[0] rather than a record actually at `candidate`. Found by sweeping for the pattern after the first two — the sweep is why it is three and not two.

The canary asserts the auto-merge workflow source matches /-m "\$\{SUBJECT\}/ — an IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE. The workflow on claude/resume-consumer-session-qm3v7c satisfies the RULE (it builds MERGE_MSG="${SUBJECT} [merge ${BRANCH}]" and commits with it, subject-first as required) but a refactor moved the value into an intermediate variable, so the canary reddens against a workflow that is correct. It selects its subject by current source text rather than by the property under test — that the dev merge message begins with what shipped. A second assertion in the same file measures HISTORICAL merges already in the log, so it has no green state reachable by any present action.

A canary asserting the envelope has exactly ONE home on DevLoopState counted occurrences of the bare string 'invariantEnvelope' in types/devCommandCenter.ts. The import specifier `from './invariantEnvelope'` also contains that string, so the count was 2 and the canary failed against correct code. Repaired to count FIELD DECLARATIONS (/^\s*invariantEnvelope\??:/gm) — the construct actually under test. THE INFORMATIVE PART: this was authored in Homecoming III Phase 1 by an agent that had cited this very invariant in the same session. A known-but-unmechanised invariant does not bind.

notes: Operator-added 2026-08-03, verbatim: "A regression test must select its subject by the property under test, not by incidental ordering, index, fixture position or current registry shape."

CHILD of CI-2026-08-03-CANARY-REPRODUCES-DEFECT-001. Hierarchy:  CANARY-REPRODUCES-DEFECT  └── CANARY-SUBJECT-SELECTION. Recorded as a child rather than a peer for the same reason IDENTIFIER-RECOVERY-CONTRACT was: it is an application of the parent, not an independent claim.

Three occurrences at ONE site (this test file), so it does NOT meet the >=2-distinct-sites bar for `validated`. Deliberately left at `candidate`: the rule is almost certainly general, but its evidence so far is not. Recurrence elsewhere is what would earn promotion — and an agent may not ratify.

Discovered minutes after the parent was ratified, by the parent applying to its own instrument: a green test that had silently stopped testing its subject is exactly "instrument failure, not protection".

OCCURRENCE SITES BROADENED 2026-08-15. The first three occurrences were all in tests/resolution-records.test.ts — thin support for a 'cross-capability' scope claim, since one file is one site. Two further occurrences now sit in tests/dev-merge-message-discipline.test.ts (a CI workflow canary) and tests/invariant-envelope-contract.test.ts (a type-contract canary), in unrelated capabilities. The scope claim is materially better evidenced than it was; whether that reaches 'validated' is the operator's call, not this record's.
